objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and manage a patient presenting with vulvar itching and discomfort.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’ve had severe itching of my vulva for about a year, and sex has become very painful over time. Over-the-counter lubricants haven’t helped much.
What is your age, and have you gone through menopause?
I’m 60 years old, and I’ve been through menopause—about 8 years ago.
Have you noticed any visible changes to the skin of your vulva, such as white patches, thinning, or areas where the skin looks different than it used to?
I haven’t noticed any obvious white patches, open sores, or widespread changes elsewhere on my skin. It mainly feels very itchy and sore, and the discomfort makes intercourse increasingly painful.
Have you noticed vaginal dryness, burning with urination, or any vaginal discharge (and if so, what does it look like)?

“I do feel some vaginal dryness, and sometimes there’s a burning sensation when I urinate, but I don’t have much to describe in the way of discharge—there hasn’t been any significant new or unusual discharge.” “The main issues are the persistent vulvar itching and the soreness, which makes sex painful.”
Have you noticed if the itching is worse at night, or have you experienced any tearing, cracking, or fissures of the skin with minor friction or sex?
“It does tend to be worse at night, and sometimes after sex I notice small areas that feel raw or slightly torn, with some cracking when there’s friction.”

Have you noticed any changes in the structure or shape of your vulvar anatomy, such as the inner lips (labia minora) becoming smaller, fused together, or the opening of the vagina appearing tighter or smaller than before?

“I haven’t noticed the labia minora fusing or getting smaller, and I don’t think the opening has changed shape or size—mostly it feels sore, very itchy, and easily gets raw or cracked with friction, especially around sex.”
Have you tried any prescription treatments, such as vaginal estrogen creams or corticosteroid ointments, or been evaluated by a gynecologist for this condition?

I haven’t tried any prescription treatments yet, and I haven’t been evaluated by a gynecologist specifically for this. I’ve only used over-the-counter lubricants, which didn’t give me significant relief.
Have you looked closely at the skin with a mirror and noticed if it appears unusually pale/white, shiny, thin, or reddened compared to the surrounding skin, even if there are no obvious "patches"?

“I haven’t done a very detailed mirror exam myself, but when I’ve looked the vulvar skin often seems a bit reddened in places and slightly more sensitive than it used to be. I don’t recall any definite thick white patches or shiny, extremely thin-looking areas.”

Given the persistent itching, tearing with friction, and postmenopausal status, have you noticed any small, raised bumps, erosions, or areas where the skin looks scratched or excoriated from rubbing or scratching?

Patient: I don’t really see clear small raised bumps or erosions like sores, but I do notice areas that look a bit more red and “scratched up” after I’ve been itching or after sex, with tenderness and raw spots. It’s mainly the itch and soreness that lead to the skin getting irritated.
Have you noticed any bleeding after intercourse, any new lumps or thickened areas on the vulva, or any sores/ulcers that don't seem to heal?

I haven’t noticed any bleeding after intercourse, and I don’t feel any new lumps or thickened areas on the vulva. I also haven’t seen any ulcers or open sores that would fail to heal—I mostly get redness and raw, irritated spots when I’ve been itching or after sex.
[DDX] Genitourinary Syndrome of Menopause (Vulvovaginal Atrophy), Lichen Sclerosus, Chronic Irritant or Allergic Contact Dermatitis, Vulvodynia (Provoked), Erosive Lichen Planus
